newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian insurance giant in major restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Colombian insurance giant in major restructuring.

text.p: Colombian insurance giant Suramericana de Seguros said Friday it plans to separate its three sub-divisions and create a fourth company dedicated to the handling its corporate investments.

Fernando Ojalvo, Suramericana's administrative vice president, said the restructuring would not involve a share split. Speaking in a telephone interview with Reuters, he also said it was not immediately clear if the new investment arm of Suramericana would be publicly traded.
Suramericanais owned by the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.
Ojalvo said the restructuring would be proposed at a shareholders' meetings set for April 17.

The company currently operates as an umbrella group comprising three business units. The units are Compania Suramericana de Seguros de Vida SA, its life insurance division; Compania Suramericana de Capitalizacion SA, the branch responsible for capitalization issues; and Administradora Suramericana de Inversiones SA, a unit set up to handle investments made by third parties or insurance clients.
Ojalvo said formal divisions would be drawn between the three units in a bid "to gave greater transparency to the investment fund, insurance and capitalization businesses."
By drawing formal lines between the three units, Suramericana's executive directors would be better able to evaluate the operating performance of each one.

He stressed that all three units and the newly created investment wing of Suramericana, would still be run by the company's board and all would continue contributing to its bottom line in terms of net profit.
